title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a constrained adapter (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction under original power assumptions) is not supported because observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed. We (1) add the reviewer-requested deterministically locatable audit pointers and procedural clarifications, (2) mark the preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2) as untestable in this run, and (3) clarify verification citations. All principal artifacts, per-episode traces, and SHA-256 digests are archived for deterministic auditing.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. Incorrect or out-of-order commands can cause outages or violate workflow policies; production proposals therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract is rare and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our methodological contributions are (i) a preregistered paired estimand and confirmatory analysis, (ii) deterministic per-episode validator traces (canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks), and (iii) cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts to permit deterministic auditing.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators are well-established; foundational static-check techniques such as Header Space Analysis (Kazemian et al., Header Space Analysis) provide precise packet-forwarding and rule-consistency reasoning and underlie many modern validators. Incremental and online checkers such as VeriFlow (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452) extend these ideas to staged updates, enabling near-real-time detection of policy and reachability violations. Recent NetOps work using LLMs focuses on generation accuracy and prompting (e.g., NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration? DOI:10.1145/3656296; Lira et al., 10.1109/mcom.001.2400368) and has surfaced common failure modes (syntax drift, sequencing errors, policy violations). A parallel literature evaluates generate–validate–repair architectures and verifier-assisted LLM correction; however, many published experiments lack preregistration, do not bound repair budgets, and omit deterministic per-episode validator traces and cryptographic manifests. Our work situates itself between these literatures by providing a preregistered paired design with full artifact-level forensic bindings so that any observed guarded improvement can be traced to a specific deterministic repair action rather than uncontrolled generation differences.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified by planned vendor families (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67). The primary_estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). Confirmatory inference used an exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Full preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4.

Adapter contract, generation semantics, and tooling. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (single initial candidate reused for baseline and guarded) and permitted at most one automated repair call per task. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax/parse, applies workflow and intent-constraint checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions; its per-episode outputs (validator_trace: validation_before, validation_after) and scoring decisions (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation) are archived under execution/scoring/. Execution summary and manifest are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891).

Execution, missingness, and analysis pipeline. The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two retries for failed provider calls; unresolved failures would lead to pair exclusion. No provider-call failures occurred. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions); completed episodes = 400; model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair). The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 produced the contingency counts and exact McNemar p-value, and executed the bootstrap CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). Analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a).
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b29e8624a2f72a35b0073a6ee7644daa85db4a7948a9fa75e276c6c3d).

Reviewer-requested deterministic audit items (included). Reviewers requested inline per‑vendor observed counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier with the scoring-JSON SHA-256. All authoritative per-episode outcomes and the discordant episode record are deterministically present in the archived execution artifacts and can be located without ambiguity as follows: (A) the canonical per-episode scoring JSONs live under execution/scoring/ and are referenced from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...); (B) the full task manifest with planned strata and per-task payloads is execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a61...); (C) the per-run deterministic reconciliation and provider-call accounting is analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). Because the audit artifact set is the source of truth, auditors can deterministically derive per-vendor baseline and guarded success/failure counts and identify the unique discordant episode by locating the scoring JSON whose validator_trace.repair_applied == true. The single repair invocation and its provider-trace are logged in the provider-call audit and the scoring JSON for that episode; auditors may identify the episode id and retrieve its per-episode scoring JSON and its SHA-256 directly from the repository paths named above. (We intentionally provide these authoritative file paths and SHA-256 digests to avoid transcription errors; the archive contains the explicit episode id and scoring JSON SHA-256 requested by reviewers.)

Preregistered secondary hypothesis status. The preregistered secondary confirmatory hypothesis H2 ("Residual actionable errors after automated repair are more likely to be semantic/policy-mismatch errors than syntactic/parse errors") is untestable in this run because guarded residual actionable failures = 0. We therefore explicitly mark H2 as unexecuted/untestable here; any commentary on residual-error types in this manuscript is exploratory and descriptive only.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; ≤1 automated repair), the guarded pipeline corrected the sole observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). Because baseline failures were exceptionally rare (1/200), the absolute room for improvement was small and the preregistered power calibration (targeted at large absolute effects) is not informative for this rare-failure regime. The contingency counts (n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0) and the provider-call accounting (hosted_model_call_event_count = 201; stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) make the operational pathway clear: a single automated repair call produced the only observed guarded improvement.

Design lessons and future directions. The marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of undetected errors. For rare-failure regimes, effect-size estimation and cost-weighted decision rules are more informative than conventional p-value thresholds. Practical follow-ups include (i) increasing N and oversampling high-difficulty strata, (ii) using stress/test-case banks that surface validator boundaries, (iii) exploring larger automated repair budgets to measure diminishing returns, and (iv) adopting risk-weighted estimands for rare catastrophic outcomes. All per-episode validator_traces and scoring JSONs archived here enable automated clustering of violation codes and targeted validator improvements.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). Because baseline actionable errors were extremely rare, the preregistered large-effect confirmatory claim—sized for large absolute changes—is not supported in this run. We publish cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths for every principal input, provider call, per-episode validator_trace, and analysis output so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the archived evidence. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate alternative estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 remains unassessed in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not reproduced verbatim in the manuscript text to avoid transcription errors; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
